clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3, effect 1 and effect 2: the interpreter and native differences of cycle 25 cases 1369 and 1528 come from the harness host reading freed code memory, not from Monad VM state.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work/src/harness.cpp:234-244: exec_code takes a reference to w.code[recipient] and builds the runtime Context with a span over code.data(). Host::call at harness.cpp:411-426 copies World into snap and assigns w = snap when the call fails, which destroys and rebuilds each map value, so the span of a frame still running points at a freed vector buffer. vg-big.err shows 50 contexts of invalid reads from copy_impl (the CODECOPY routine) at 9,493 bytes inside a freed 9,537 byte block, and vg-big-5rep.txt shows SAME with gasleft 149618850 on both engines in all five repetitions. A linear opcode scan of research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (24,009 runtime bytes) finds no 0x39 CODECOPY and no 0x3c EXTCODECOPY, so no PoolManager result came from freed code. In the node, vm.cpp:83-84 builds the Context from icode->code_span() and code.hpp:36-62 holds the Intercode in a shared_ptr carried by Varcode, so the node does not have this fault. The cleared item stands.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 4: places where the interpreter and native code of v0.16.5 could differ by design (whole block static gas charged on entry, deferred sign check, base gas added back before CALL and SSTORE sentry) cannot change persisted PoolManager state.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.cpp:443-448 (block base gas decremented on entry), runtime/call.cpp:136-154 (gas_left_here = gas_remaining + remaining_block_base_gas before the 63/64 rule, depth check shared), runtime/storage.cpp:70-73 (EIP-2200 sentry uses the same add back) and runtime/context.cpp:174-176 (negative gas_remaining at STOP, RETURN or REVERT becomes out of gas). A block that the interpreter cannot finish also fails in native code, and the child gas given to a CALL is computed from the same value on both engines, so the CALL forwards the same gas. The only difference is where inside a failing frame the failure happens, and the failing frame is reverted on both engines with all gas consumed. I found no case where a frame succeeds on one engine and fails on the other. The cleared item stands.
